Peloponnesian War: War between Athens and Sparta (431–404 BC). The war consists of four related conflicts which have traditionally been combined into one.
Founded in 1967 by George Habash, this Marxist-Leninist faction pioneered airplane hijackings and remains the second-largest group within the PLO after Fatah. Which organization?
Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine

Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine: Palestinian Marxist–Leninist organization. It has consistently been the second-largest of the groups forming the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), the largest being Fatah.
Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine

Employed to paint glow-in-the-dark watch dials in the 1910s and 1920s, these American factory workers were told to point their brushes with their lips — ingesting a radioactive element that would reshape U.S. labor law. Who were they?
Radium Girls: American female radiation poisoning victims (1917–1978)
Known by the abbreviation PRO and led by former Argentine president Mauricio Macri, which party has governed Buenos Aires since 2007?
Republican Proposal: Political party in Argentina.
This granddaughter of a Michigan governor chaired the Republican National Committee from 2017 until resigning in 2024, presiding over a string of election losses — who is she?
This Nazirite judge of ancient Israel slew a lion with his bare hands and later routed a Philistine army using only a donkey's jawbone — who was he?
Samson: Important character from the book of judges of the Hebrew Bible.
Nicknamed both "the Blond" and "the Drunkard," this son of Suleiman the Magnificent saw Cyprus and Tunis conquered but suffered a famous naval loss at Lepanto — who was he?
Selim II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1566 to 1574.
Eldest daughter of King Amalric, this 12th-century ruler stood by her unpopular husband Guy of Lusignan even as her leprosy-stricken brother struggled to secure her succession — who is she?
Sibylla, Queen of Jerusalem: Crusader ruler from 1186 to 1190.

Traditionally blamed on Queen Catherine de' Medici, this 1572 wave of Catholic mob violence targeted Huguenots gathered in Paris for a royal wedding during the French Wars of Religion. By what name is it known?
St. Bartholomew's Day massacre: 1572 killing of Huguenots in France.

Widely regarded as one of the greatest Roman historians, this writer chronicled the empire from Augustus's death to Domitian's reign in two major works, and also penned an account of his general father-in-law's campaigns in Britain — who was he?

Beginning in 73 BCE with about 70 gladiators escaping a school in Capua, this slave revolt swelled to 120,000 people and became the only such uprising to directly threaten the Roman heartland — what was it called?
Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula
Third Servile War: 73–71 BCE Roman slave rebellion.
This second emperor of Vietnam's Trần dynasty handed the throne to his son yet stayed on as 'retired emperor,' co-commanding the victories that repelled two Mongol invasions of Đại Việt — who was he?
Trần Thánh Tông: Emperor of Đại Việt from 1258 to 1278.
Elected in 2000, this businessman-turned-politician became the first Mexican president since 1929 who wasn't from the long-dominant PRI party. Who broke that streak?
Vicente Fox: President of Mexico from 2000 to 2006.
Generally marked by widespread violence and destruction, this armed conflict between states or organized groups is typically waged in pursuit of political, economic, or territorial aims — what is it?
War: Intense armed conflict. It is generally characterized by widespread violence, destruction, and mortality, using regular or irregular military forces.

An explorer, lawyer and one of colonial New South Wales' wealthiest figures, he co-founded Australia's first independent newspaper and championed emancipists, trial by jury and self-government — who was he?
William Wentworth: Australian statesman, writer and explorer.
The only Israeli soldier killed during a daring 1976 hostage-rescue raid on a hijacked airliner in Uganda, he was the elder brother of a future Israeli prime minister — who was he?
Which of these people was born first?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four. Python supports multiple programming paradigms but with an emphasis on object-oriented programming and dynamic typing.
Which one below was established earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Robert Boyle is a physicist. Robert Boyle (25 January 1627 – 31 December 1691) was an Anglo-Irish natural philosopher, chemist, physicist, alchemist and inventor.
Pick the chemist from these four.
James Lovelock is a chemist. James Ephraim Lovelock (26 July 1919 – 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
What is the atomic number of Neodymium?
Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
In what year was Pythagoras born?
Pythagoras: Pythagoras of Samos (Ancient Greek: Πυθαγόρας; c. 570 – c. 495 BC) was an ancient Ionian Greek philosopher, polymath, and the eponymous founder of Pythagoreanism.
In what year was Elon Musk born?
Elon Musk: Elon Reeve Musk (EE-lon; born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
In what year was Armin Meiwes born?
Armin Meiwes: After Meiwes and the victim jointly attempted to eat the victim's severed penis, Meiwes murdered his victim and proceeded to eat a large amount of his flesh.
In what year did Mohamed Atta die?
Mohamed Atta: In Hamburg, Atta attended prayers at the al-Quds Mosque where he met Marwan al-Shehhi, Ramzi bin al-Shibh, and Ziad Jarrah, with whom he formed the Hamburg cell.
In what year did Nostradamus die?
Nostradamus's father's family had originally been Jewish, but had converted to Catholic Christianity a generation before Nostradamus was born.
In what year was Silver discovered?
Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
In what year was Manganese discovered?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
Which company manufactures LTV A-7 Corsair II?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: Ling-Temco-Vought. The LTV A-7 Corsair II is an American carrier-capable subsonic light attack aircraft designed and manufactured by Ling-Temco-Vought (LTV).
Which country is Sukhoi Su-57 from?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russia. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Who is credited with discovering Grus?
Grus (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Grus (or colloquially) is a constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Reynolds number?
Reynolds number: Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet. At low Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be dominated by laminar (sheet-like) flow, while at high Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be turbulent.
Who is credited with discovering Ceres?
Ceres (dwarf planet): Giuseppe Piazzi. Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
This localized collection of pus builds up within body tissue, usually from bacterial infection, causing redness, pain, warmth, and swelling. What is it?
Abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
A pioneer of industrial toxicology, this American physician trained at Michigan, worked out of Hull House in Chicago, and led the fight to curb lead poisoning in the workplace — who was she?
Alice Hamilton (February 27, 1869 - September 22, 1970) was an American physician, research scientist, and author.

This American anthropologist specialized in the economic anthropology and rural development of Indonesia, earning her PhD from the University of Hawaii in 1992 after studying women's weaving and blacksmithing on Java. Who was she?
Ann Dunham (November 29, 1942 - November 7, 1995) was an American anthropologist who specialized in the economic anthropology and rural development of Indonesia.
Named from Greek words for 'even' and 'toe,' this mammal order bears its weight equally on two of its five toes, unlike its odd-toed counterpart — what order is it?
Artiodactyla (from Ancient Greek rtios 'even' and dktylos 'finger, toe') is an order of placental mammals.
Native to Europe, this small white-petaled, yellow-centered lawn flower is called 'common,' 'lawn,' or 'English' in various regions — what is its scientific name?
Bellis perennis (p-), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy.
Recognised by South Africa's Kennel Union but not by the international federation, this large, muscular mastiff-type breed serves as a family guard dog — name it?
Boerboel is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
This English-like, compiled programming language was designed for business use and remains widely used today to maintain legacy mainframe systems in banking and government — what language is it?
COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which metabolic process is the polar opposite of anabolism, breaking large molecules such as proteins and lipids down into monomers while releasing energy, some of it lost as heat?
Catabolism is the set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units that are either oxidized to release energy or used in other anabolic reactions.
The first element in group 6, it lends its name to the shiny plating on car bumpers and, mixed into steel, makes it stainless. Which steely-grey metal is it?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
This term describes all the material inside a cell's outer membrane, excluding the nucleus (in cells that have one) — its main components include a gel-like fluid called the cytosol. What is it?
Cytoplasm is all the material within a eukaryotic or prokaryotic cell, enclosed by the cell membrane, including the organelles and excluding the nucleus in eukaryotic cells.

Bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba, Argentina, for hunting big game like wild boar and pumas, this large mastiff-type dog breed traces its ancestry partly to a now-extinct fighting dog — name the breed?
Dogo Argentino (plural Dogos Argentinos) is an Argentine breed of large dog of mastiff type.
Many of these Northern Hemisphere shade trees, prized along old European and American streets, were wiped out by a fungus carried by bark beetles — which tree genus is this?
Elm are deciduous and semi-deciduous trees comprising the genus Ulmus in the family Ulmaceae.

The telltale earth mounds this tunneling mammal pushes to the surface come from its constantly expanding burrow system, and it feeds mainly on earthworms paralyzed by toxins in its saliva — what animal is it?
European mole (Talpa europaea) is a mammal of the order Eulipotyphla.

This genetic neurodevelopmental disorder causes a long, narrow face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, with males typically far more affected than females and average IQ under 55 in affected boys — what's the condition?

Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder. The average IQ in males with FXS is under 55, while affected females tend to be in the borderline to normal range, typically around 70–85.

This heavy, slow-moving reptile native to the southwestern US and northwestern Mexico is the only venomous lizard found in the United States, though its sluggish nature makes it rarely dangerous — what animal is it?
Gila monster (Heloderma suspectum) is a species of venomous lizard native to the Southwestern United States and the northwestern Mexican state of Sonora.
This eel-shaped ocean scavenger defends itself by flooding predators with slime from glands in its skin — what creature is it?
Hagfish (also known as Hyperotreti) and order Myxiniformes, are eel-shaped jawless fish (occasionally called slime eels).
Also called the ratel, this animal is Africa's largest land-dwelling mustelid, armed with remarkably loose skin that lets it twist around and bite back even when grabbed. What is it?
Honey badger (Mellivora capensis), also known as the ratel (or), is a mammal widely distributed across Africa, Southwest Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.
This Russian-American aviation pioneer, a trailblazer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft, won the top prize at the 1912 Moscow Aviation Exhibition for one of his early designs — who is he?
Igor Sikorsky (25 May 1889 - 26 October 1972) was a Russian-American aviation pioneer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft.
With brownish-grey fur and a pinkish-red face, this cold-hardy primate is known colloquially by a wintry nickname referencing the snow in its habitat — which species?
Japanese macaque (Macaca fuscata), also known as the snow monkey, is a terrestrial Old World monkey species that is native to Japan.
This Hungarian-American biochemist spent years pushing past skepticism to lay the groundwork for mRNA vaccines, winning a 2023 Nobel alongside Drew Weissman. Who is she?

Katalin Karikó (born 17 January 1955) is a Hungarian and American biochemist who specializes in ribonucleic acid (RNA)-mediated mechanisms, particularly in vitro-transcribed messenger RNA (mRNA) for protein replacement therapy.

Which citrus-scented perennial herb in the mint family, whose genus name Melissa comes from the Greek for 'honey bee,' is naturalized worldwide after originating in the Mediterranean and Central Asia?
Lemon balm (Melissa officinalis) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the mint family.
Dubbed the 'Queen of QVC' for her long-running shopping show and holding over 120 patents, this American entrepreneur is also an investor on the reality series Shark Tank — who is she?
Lori Greiner is an American television personality and entrepreneur.

A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered a new element in 1939 by purifying lanthanum laced with actinium, and went on to become the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Marguerite Perey (19 October 1909 - 13 May 1975) was a French physicist and a student of Marie Curie.
This British-Lebanese geometer co-founded topological K-theory and lent his name to a famous index theorem — and won both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize. Who was he?
Michael Atiyah (22 April 1929 - 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.
This small green legume, cultivated widely across East and South Asia, is used in both savory dishes and sweet desserts — what is it?
Mung bean (Vigna radiata) is a plant species in the legume family.
Born in the Austro-Hungarian Empire and emigrating to the US in 1884, he's known for pioneering the AC electricity system. Who?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 - 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
This specialized subunit within a biological cell performs a specific function, and may be enclosed in its own membrane or exist without one. What is it?
Organelle is a specialized subunit, within a biological cell, that has a specific function.
Born in the Soviet Union, this entrepreneur co-founded a Russian social network before creating a messaging app with his brother and later relocating to Dubai — who is he?
Pavel Durov (born 10 October 1984) is a technology entrepreneur.

Derived from phosphoric acid by removing one to three protons, this anion or salt takes forms like dihydrogen and hydrogen variants and gives its name to fertilizers and various esters — name the ion?
Phosphate is an anion, salt, functional group or ester derived from a phosphoric acid.
This spiny rodent actually comes in two unrelated varieties, an Old World family and a New World family, whose lookalike coats of keratin quills evolved independently — what animal is it?
Porcupine are large rodents with coats of sharp spines, or quills, that protect them against predators.
This opening at the center of the iris lets light reach the retina and appears black — round in people, a slit in cats, and even a ring shape in some catfish — what's it called?
Pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.
Also called king's crown or Arctic root, this Arctic-growing perennial is widely sold as a supplement even though regulators say its health claims lack solid evidence — which plant?
Rhodiola rosea (commonly golden root, rose root, roseroot, Aaron's rod, Arctic root, king's crown, lignum rhodium, orpin rose) is a perennial flowering plant in the family Crassulaceae.
Once placed in its own plant family before molecular studies folded it into Dracaena, this African and Asian succulent genus includes the plant nicknamed 'devil's tongue' — which genus?

Sansevieria is a historically recognized genus of flowering plants, native to Africa, notably Madagascar, and southern Asia, now included in the genus Dracaena on the basis of molecular phylogenetic studies.
Believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso, this toy dog breed originated in Tibet — name the breed?
Shih Tzu is a toy dog or pet dog breed originating from Tibet and believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso.
Usually diagnosed in infancy, this rare genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the SMN1 gene is the leading inherited cause of death in babies if left untreated — what condition is it?
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare neuromuscular disorder that results in the loss of motor neurons and progressive muscle wasting.
Named for its long, flat, sword-like bill, this large migratory predatory fish loses all its teeth and scales by adulthood and is a popular target among billfish anglers — what is it?
Swordfish (Xiphias gladius), also known as the broadbill in some countries, are large, highly migratory predatory fish characterized by a long, flat, sword-like, pointed bill.
What common name covers a group of spike-leaved flowering plants — mostly in the daisy family — whose prickles evolved purely to ward off hungry herbivores?
Thistle is the common name of a group of flowering plants characterised by leaves with sharp spikes on the margins, mostly in the family Asteraceae.
Several highly prized truffle species belong to this fungal genus, whose lineage is estimated to date to the close of the Jurassic period — which genus?
Tuber (fungus) is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).

This English fashion designer, largely responsible for bringing punk fashion into the mainstream, ran a boutique on King's Road with her partner, whose band helped define the 1970s UK punk scene — who is she?

Vivienne Westwood (ne Swire; 8 April 1941 - 29 December 2022) was an English fashion designer and businesswoman, largely responsible for bringing modern punk and new wave fashions into the mainstream.
This Russian political activist and economist, described as the 'first lady' of her country's opposition, vowed to continue her late husband's work after fleeing into exile. Who is she?
Yulia Navalnaya (ne Abrosimova; born 24 July 1976) is a Russian political activist and economist.

A key figure of the Scottish Enlightenment, this philosopher wrote The Theory of Moral Sentiments before the 1776 work often called the inception of modern economics — who is the "father of economics"?
Adam Smith: Scottish economist and philosopher (1723–1790)
Belonging to the birch family and found throughout the north temperate zone, this genus of about 35 tree and shrub species even reaches into the Andes — what genus is it?
Alder: Genus of flowering plants in the birch family Betulaceae.
Sold under the brand name Norvasc, this long-acting calcium channel blocker treats high blood pressure and variant angina by relaxing and widening the arteries — what's the drug?
Amlodipine: Medication against high blood pressure.
This British-American theoretical physicist at the University of Illinois won the 2003 Nobel Prize for pioneering work on superfluidity and the quantum physics of low-temperature helium — who was he?
Painting, sculpture, and architecture are its three classical visual branches, yet nobody can agree on a single definition for it; what cultural pursuit of creative and imaginative talent is this?
Art: Creative work to evoke aesthetic response.
The world's largest nocturnal primate, this Madagascar lemur has ever-growing rodent-like teeth and taps tree trunks with a bony middle finger to fish out grubs by echo — which animal?
Aye-aye: Species of primate. This foraging method is called percussive foraging, and takes up 5–41% of the aye-aye's foraging time.
Named after the aromatic resin from which it was first derived, this simplest aromatic carboxylic compound forms salts widely used as food preservatives — what is it called?
Believed to descend from hounds once kept at a Belgian abbey, this scent hound can follow a human trail days old and is a favorite of police tracking escaped prisoners — which breed is it?
Bloodhound: Dog breed used for tracking by scent.
Grown on one of the Amazon's largest and longest-lived trees, this selenium-rich edible seed comes in a shell weighing up to 2 kilograms combined with its fruit. What is it?
Brazil nut: Species of tree and its edible seeds.
Native to tropical Africa, this gourd-producing vine yields fruit that can be eaten young as a vegetable or dried and hollowed out into bowls, ladles, or even musical instruments — what is it?
Calabash: Species of bottle gourd plant.
Ranked the world's richest person by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, this Mexican tycoon built his fortune largely through telecommunications and remains Latin America's wealthiest individual — who is he?
Around 20 millimetres long with a shimmering structural-green shell and a coppery underside, this beetle is identified by its isosceles-triangle scutellum — which species?
Cetonia aurata: Species of beetle. The scutellum is the small V-shaped area between the wing cases; it may show several small, irregular, white lines and marks.
This human-feeding ectoparasite is one of the world's great "nuisance pests" — yet despite carrying dozens of pathogens, no study has shown it transmits any disease to us. What is it?
Cimex lectularius: Species of true bug.
This umbrella term covers mental processes like perception, attention, memory, and reasoning that let us acquire and apply knowledge — what is it called?
Cognition: Mental process dealing with knowledge.
Born in 1863, this Italian is remembered as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
This herpesvirus genus's human species can cause mononucleosis in adults but birth defects affecting the eyes, ears, liver, and spleen when passed to a fetus — which virus?
Cytomegalovirus: Genus of viruses. The 11 species in this genus include Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV, HHV-5), which is the species that infects humans.
Marked by up to 20 liters of dilute urine a day and intense thirst that drinking barely satisfies, this condition comes in four types tied to problems with the hormone vasopressin — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus: Condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
Working alongside biochemist Katalin Karikó on nucleoside base modifications, this University of Pennsylvania immunologist shared the 2023 Nobel Prize for enabling COVID-19 mRNA vaccines — who is he?
Drew Weissman: American physician and immunologist (born 1959)
Named for the large trunk-like proboscis of its males, this giant oceangoing pinniped can weigh up to 4,000 kilograms and was once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil. What animal is it?
Elephant seal: Genus of aquatic carnivores.
Sold under the brand name Nexium, this proton pump inhibitor treats acid reflux by blocking an enzyme in the stomach's acid-producing cells — what is it?
Esomeprazole: Medication which reduces stomach acid.
Co-founder and CEO of Snap Inc., this businessman was the youngest billionaire in the world back in 2015 — who is he?

Boldly patterned in black and yellow to warn predators of its toxicity, this European amphibian can live for more than 50 years and is now vulnerable due to an introduced fungal disease — what species is it?
Fire salamander: Species of amphibian. The fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) is a common species of salamander found in Europe.
Often bonded to glucose to form sucrose, this simple sugar is found in honey, fruit, and most root vegetables — which sugar?
Fructose: Simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants.

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
Born from an accidental 18th-century cross between the sweet orange and the pomelo in Barbados, this citrus hybrid is nicknamed the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit: Citrus fruit. The grapefruit (Citrus × paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.
The best-known of these rodents is the golden or Syrian species, though dwarf varieties like Campbell's and the Roborovski are popular too — what small pet is this?
Named after the 19th-century physicist who proved electromagnetic waves exist, which SI unit measures one cycle per second?
Hertz: SI unit of frequency. The hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.
This condition involves a buildup of cerebrospinal fluid around the brain, causing headaches, vision problems, and in babies a rapidly enlarging head — what is it?
Hydrocephalus: Abnormal increase in cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.
Powered by four Aviadvigatel turbofans and built in Voronezh, this Soviet-designed wide-body jet now serves mainly as the Russian president's aircraft — which airliner?
Ilyushin Il-96: Russian four-engined long-range wide-body jet airliner.
Resembling a mustelid despite being a wild cat, this Americas-native feline comes in gray or red color morphs and once roamed as far north as Texas — which species?
Jaguarundi: Species of felid. Its range extends from central Argentina in the south and much of South America east of the Andes, through Central America, and into northern Mexico.
He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987, then later urged people to uninstall the product bearing his name and twice ran for U.S. president — who was he?
John McAfee: British and American programmer and businessman (1945–2021)
With an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters and a record of 5.85 meters, this snake is the world's longest venomous species, endemic to Asia. What is it?
King cobra: Group of venomous snakes from Asia.
Weighing up to 1,100 pounds, this heaviest of all non-crocodilian reptiles lacks a bony shell, its carapace covered instead in oily, leather-like flesh — what animal is it?
Leatherback sea turtle: Species of marine reptile.
Defined as exactly one cubic decimetre and rooted in an old French unit called the litron, what metric measure of volume is this?
Litre: Unit of volume. The litre (Commonwealth spelling) or liter (American spelling) (SI symbols L and l, other symbol used: ℓ) is a metric unit of volume.
A Russian linguist by training, this woman served two separate terms as first lady of Russia, from 2000 to 2008 and again from 2012 to 2014 — who is she?
Lyudmila Putina: Ex-wife of Vladimir Putin (born 1958)
Prized for its sweet, pine-and-citrus flavor, this perennial herb is often considered synonymous with oregano in parts of the Middle East — what is it?
Marjoram: Perennial herb. It is also called pot marjoram, although this name is also used for other cultivated species of Origanum.
This mammal family — skunks and stink badgers — was reclassified out of the weasel family in the 1990s after genetic evidence, and turns out to be closest kin to red pandas and raccoons. What is it?
Mephitidae: Family of mammals. In taxonomic order, the living species of Mephitidae are:.
Soviet pilots nicknamed this 1972 gunship the 'flying tank,' a helicopter NATO calls 'Hind' that can also haul eight troops and still flies in 52 countries. What is it?
Mil Mi-24: Family of assault and attack helicopters.
Forming dense green mats with leaves just one cell thick, these seedless plants reproduce via spore-topped stalks called sporophytes — which plants?
Moss: Division of typically non-vascular land plants.
The sole surviving family of an ancient cephalopod lineage, these nine living species carry coiled chambered shells 10 to 25 cm across and are all protected under CITES — what creatures are they?
Nautilus: Family of molluscs. It comprises nine living species in two genera, the type of which is the genus Nautilus.
This American physicist won the 1989 Nobel for inventing the separated oscillatory field method behind atomic clocks, and helped found both Brookhaven National Laboratory and Fermilab — who was he?
Colloquially called harvestmen or daddy long legs, this arachnid order looks startlingly modern in 400-million-year-old fossils from Scotland's Rhynie cherts — what is it?
Opiliones: Order of arachnids. The Opiliones (formerly Phalangida) are an order of arachnids, colloquially known as harvestmen, harvesters, daddy long legs, or granddaddy long legs.

Sold over the counter under brand names like Tylenol and Panadol, this analgesic eases mild migraines and tension headaches but is famously inferior to ibuprofen at knocking down a fever — what is it?
Paracetamol: Medication for pain and fever.
By learning to synthesize hormones from plant sterols — even wild Mexican yams — this research chemist laid the foundation for cortisone and the birth-control pill. Who was this pioneer?
Percy Lavon Julian: American research chemist (1899–1975)

For two thousand years it lived inside natural philosophy alongside chemistry and biology, only breaking off as its own discipline during the 17th-century Scientific Revolution; what is this study of matter, energy, and force?
Physics: Scientific field of study. It is one of the most fundamental scientific disciplines.
Built from many linked simple sugars and including starch, glycogen, and cellulose among its examples, this class of carbohydrate is the most abundant in our food — what is it called?
Polysaccharide: Long carbohydrate polymers such as starch, glycogen, cellulose, and chitin.
Known by folk names like 'bird cherry' and 'Mayday tree,' this flowering plant in the rose family is native to Europe and northern Asia — what species is it?
Prunus padus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
What term describes an atom, molecule, or ion with at least one unpaired valence electron, making it highly reactive and prone to processes like dimerization or polymerization?
Radical (chemistry): Atom, molecule, or ion that has an unpaired valence electron; typically highly reactive.
Discovered in 1803 by William Hyde Wollaston and named for the rose color of one of its compounds, this rare silvery-white metal of the platinum group is used to enhance jewelry — which element?
Rhodium: Chemical element with atomic number 45 (Rh)
Extremely cold-hardy and thriving in poor soil, this cereal grass is a staple grain behind Scandinavian crispbread and a certain whiskey style — what is it?
Rye: Species of grain. Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
A predatory arachnid with eight legs, grasping pincers and a stinger-tipped tail, this desert-loving hunter has a lineage going back some 430 million years to the Silurian — what is it?
Made up of the collarbone, the scapula, and the upper-arm bone meeting in a ball-and-socket joint, which body part lets the arm swing in a full circle?
Shoulder: Part of the body. The articulations between the bones of the shoulder make up the shoulder joints.
This frozen dessert blends ice with fruit juice or purée — and sometimes wine, liqueur, or honey — for a refreshing icy treat. What is it called?
